messages.author: 2dc50513792871a4
messages.subject: Shiny Server as non-root
parts:
Hi,

This is my first time posting to the Shiny google group, so first of all, thank you so much for developing Shiny. It has really enhanced my workflow, not to mention made it much easier to convince non-statisticians that statistics is cool and fun!

Our organization is hoping to use the Shiny server to host our own Shiny apps. We want to run shiny-server as a non-root user. It looks like this functionality has been implemented in this github branch:

https://github.com/jcheng5/shiny-server/tree/no-su

But we are eager for this functionality to be included in an official release. I thought it would be worth mentioning that this is an important and much desired capability for a really great piece of software. As the stats person who has been making apps with Shiny since January, all seems well and good. But not being a web/IT person, I am pretty much just quoting the needs/wants of others where I work who are more involved in secure web deployment. So unfortunately, I can't comment much on why this is so important, but this is just to let you guys know that it does seem to be our one and only obstacle to using Shiny publicly rather than just on a local development server. Is there any cause for concern or inconveniences over using the github branch above? In terms of eventually having to switch at some point later on from that branch to a later release of shiny-server?

Thanks so much,
Matt

I'm working with Matt on this, and forgive me if this is a stupid question, but it's not clear to us how to properly install shiny-server using the github files. I originally installed a release version of shiny-server using the instructions on this page:

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server

/usr/local/lib/node_modules/shiny-server/

wget https://github.com/jcheng5/shiny-server/archive/no-su.tar.gz
tar xzf no-su.tar.gz
cd shiny-server-no-su
sudo npm install -g .
